Gather trusted calculations and context

Source: R/commons.R
commons.Rd

commons() gathers a team's data sources, semantic layer, and context layer into one object, "the commons", that code can call directly without a model. Pass it to agent() to build an agent in R, or place it in an R session that a coding agent already controls.

Usage

commons(..., data_sources, semantic_layer = NULL, context_layer = NULL)

Arguments

...

These dots are for future extensions and must be empty.

data_sources

A data_source(), or a named list of them. Measures can take a source's connection as an argument named after the source; see semantic_layer().

semantic_layer

An optional semantic_layer().

context_layer

An optional context_layer().

Value

A commons object with methods:

  • $search(query) searches trusted calculations.

  • $measure(name, arguments) runs a measure.

  • $metrics(metrics, dimensions, filters, where, arguments, source) computes governed metrics. where takes simple conditions on documented columns, either as a string like "project = 'dplyr' AND date >= '2026-06-01'" or as a list of c(column, op, value) triples.

  • $calculation(name, arguments, source) runs an exact trusted query.

  • $context(query) searches trusted context.

  • $describe(table, source) describes a table.

  • $run_sql(query, source) runs a read-only query and returns a data frame. Governed definitions can be written as {{name}} tokens (or {{table::name}} when qualification is needed), and each expands to its compiled SQL before the query runs.

Details

All arguments must be named.

Using commons with other coding agents

commons() is the entry point to use commons with external coding agents. The approach depends on whether the coding agent already has a persistent R session. For example, Posit Assistant connects to the user's R session. Claude Code and Codex, by contrast, do not have a built-in connection to a persistent R REPL.

For agents that already have an R session, like Posit Assistant, create a commons() object in the relevant .Rprofile and then add a line telling the agent to print it out before doing data analysis:

The R session has an object called `commons` that holds this team's trusted
code and context. Before analyzing data, run `print(commons)`, and use its
calculations where they apply in favor of writing analysis code ad-hoc.

Claude Code and Codex have no persistent R session of their own. They can get one through MCP Console. Its R session reads the project's .Rprofile like any other, so build commons there in the same way, and then edit the console tool's description to tell the model to print out commons before analyzing data.

To use MCP console, register it for the project, from the project directory:

uvx mcp-console configure-client claude --directory .
uvx mcp-console configure-client codex --directory .

Then configure MCP Console to offer the model only R, so that it queries data through commons$run_sql() rather than sending SQL to a database itself, and to mention commons in its tool description. A configured description replaces the one MCP Console generates, so start from an export of the resolved configuration:

mkdir -p .agents/console
uvx mcp-console config resolve --full --no-project-config \
  -c 'languages=[r]' > .agents/console/config.yaml

In that file, keep languages: [r], and add the same sentence to the end of the exported description:

languages:
  - r
tool:
  description: |-
    # ...the exported description, unchanged...

    The R session has an object called `commons` that holds this team's
    trusted code and context. Before analyzing data, run
    `print(commons)`, and use its calculations where they apply in favor of
    writing analysis code ad-hoc.

Claude Code shows the tool description only once the agent loads the tool, so add the sentence to the end of tool.instructions as well.

$context() needs one more step for now. This applies even without a context layer when a data source has a data dictionary or semantic model, since $context() searches those too. It relies on DuckDB's fts extension, which MCP Console's sandbox can't download. MCP Console can install the extension itself, but only into its own cache, which R's duckdb doesn't read by default. Point R at that cache with an absolute path (~ and environment variables aren't expanded):

environment:
  # macOS; on Linux, /home/you/.cache/mcp-console/dependencies/duckdb
  DUCKDB_R_HOME: /Users/you/Library/Caches/mcp-console/dependencies/duckdb

Then add one more sentence to both tool.description and tool.instructions, so the agent asks MCP Console to install the extension:

The first time you run `commons$context()`, include
`"requirements": {"duckdb": ["fts"]}` in the same call.

In either setup, $run_sql() refuses queries that write, but that check isn't a security boundary. Code that the agent runs in the same R session can reach anything the session can, including the connections behind commons. Connect to databases with a read-only role.

Lifecycle

Before commons 0.2.0, commons() built the agent itself, taking client as its first argument. Calls in that form still work, with a deprecation warning, and return an agent as before. Use agent() instead.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
commons <- commons(
  data_sources = data_source(warehouse = con),
  semantic_layer = sem,
  context_layer = context_layer(files = "notes.md")
)
commons
commons$search("revenue by region")
commons$measure("revenue_by_region", arguments = list(region = "West"))

# The same object backs an agent:
agent <- agent(ellmer::chat_anthropic(), commons = commons)
} # }
